# physical_timing_class: whether being flat is CORRECT for the process.
# A TE4 month of a continuous stock-driven process is not unresolved timing;

# current exported monthly coverage records; neither is a fixed percentage.

column14: a ruminant emits every day it is alive. The herd is a census stock with no monthly dimension, and a seasonal profile would be an invention. Days-weighting is the complete answer here

column13: VIIRS active-fire acquisition dates (held), FAO calendar as comparator
column14: Year-specific FRP-weighted VIIRS profiles are used where held detections cover the relevant crop-season windows. Fire detection is a proxy for residue-burning emissions, so the evidence class remains T3; source coverage and any substituted year are recorded by the temporal profile producer

Synthetic-fertiliser timing uses supported monthly offtake profiles. Offtake records product transfer at the dealer/depot boundary, not application at the soil. Deposited and applied livestock nitrogen, organic manure and crop residues have different pathways and retain their separately documented timing; the offtake profile is not evidence for those flows

column13: temperature, weakly: storage decay rises with heat
column14: continuous decay of a continuously replenished store. A temperature-driven variant is defensible and is a profile variant, not a correction
